cross_case_signal.interpretation: The retained six-case artifact shows the constructor self-time bucket scaling almost linearly with output entry count. This is corroborating diagnostic evidence that the inline per-entry structural admission walk, rather than O(1) identifier/semiring checks or tuple copies, is the dominant profile bucket. It is not a product benchmark or a causal performance proof.

measurement.finding: The frozen high-output case is no longer ambiguous enough to justify another instrumentation abstraction: canonical tuple inputs are reused, persisted-scalar admission is a minority profile bucket, and the dominant remaining bucket is inline TypedRelationBlock structural admission. Previous packets already fused the canonical column validation path and retained the independent row-offset type/error-precedence scan, so no safe Delete/Consolidate production edit is identified here.
measurement.scope_limit: The measurements are synthetic, CPU-only, cProfile-perturbed attribution plus independent constructor wall timing. They do not establish a general speedup, memory win, production workload crossover, GPU/Tensor-Core superiority, or Tensor-over-Forest advantage.

result.summary: GPU-99 closes the constructor attribution question without reviving retired A/B profiler paths. The frozen packed-result factory already supplies exact tuples, so immutable tuple copying is absent; retained cProfile evidence places about 93.0% of post-init cumulative time in the constructor self-time bucket and about 6.3% in Boolean scalar admission. No further safe constructor micro-refactor is justified under the existing refusal and canonicalization contracts.
